items.title: Angola Talking Interview, 1959-03-15
items.q: The interviewee refers to 'Seven-year-old boy' as his son ('he's preaching now himself... put it on your kid'), but 'Seven-year-old boy' is not a specific named person in the controlled vocabulary sense, and the relationship is familial, not musical/professional as per the likely intent of the jazz

ctx.x: Why do you want to put it down?

Well, I was thinking about looking out for a pound or so for Jesus, you know. But I looked into it in one way. I can play church songs. I can play church songs, too. That's well so than I can blues. I had so many dreams and signs that came before me. And the other way, I thought I was a Christian man before I got here. What Jesus gave me, he didn't take it away from me. I walked away from him. And he sent me to be a preacher and I didn't take it up. I was supposed to be a teacher. Well, I didn't take it up. So,…
Did you have a teacher for music?
